cands.name: Ra'Shon Young
cands.bio: Orlando Democrat, 27. Former chief of staff to LaVon Bracy Davis; won the Sept. 2025 special election with about 75%. Bethune-Cookman University graduate (2021). Described as the first Gen Z Democrat elected to the Florida Legislature.
cands.local_ties: Orlando; district covers northern Orange County (Pine Hills, Ocoee, Lockhart, College Park), per Florida Politics and the ClickOrlando guide.

record.text: Sponsored the House companion to a bill awarding $4 million to descendants of the Groveland Four, which Sen. Bracy Davis carried in the Senate; the money was added to the budget late.
Was a leading critic of the Florida SAVE Act (HB 991), calling it a "poll tax by paperwork"; the News Collaborative guide says most bills he sponsored died in committee.

money_notes.text: Raised almost $98,000 through his candidate account in the 2025 special election.
Reported $34,456 in contributions and $12,445.80 in expenditures as of Oct. 6, 2026.

cands.gaps: No donor-level reporting or endorsement list found. Wikipedia lists him as a NASA engineer, but the Florida Politics passage I read attributes a NASA engineering past to his opponent Le, so I left it out. Owner sources: one combined web search (name plus the owner-source domains) returned no hits on any of them, but the search tool did not honor the site: filter, so coverage is incomplete; alexjoneslive.com on-site search also returned no results.

votes.what: Joint resolution putting Amendment 3 (Save Our Homes property-tax changes: higher homestead exemption, lower assessment-increase limits) on the Nov 2026 ballot.

cands.name: Tuan Le
cands.bio: Apopka engineer and former restaurateur (CEO of LeNgineer and Lennovation, per Winter Garden Vox). Vietnamese immigrant raised in Pine Hills. Lost the 2025 special election to Young and two Republican congressional primaries. Has never held elected office.
cands.local_ties: Apopka resident who grew up in Pine Hills, per the Winter Garden Vox candidate profile (2025).

record.text: Chosen as Republican nominee by Orange County GOP committee members on Aug. 21, 2025 after Nate Robertson withdrew; lost the Sept. 2025 special election to Young with roughly 25% of the vote.
Lost the Republican primary for U.S. House District 10 in 2022 and 2024.

money_notes.text: Florida Politics (Oct. 29, 2026): his campaign has not done any fundraising; in 2025 he never filed a fundraising report.

controversies.text: Winter Garden Vox reported a history of evictions, tax liens and health-code violations tied to his Brevard County restaurant chain, and that his qualifying-fee check bounced and was replaced with a cashier's check. Reported by the outlet from records; Le told the outlet business challenges were a reason he wanted public office.

cands.gaps: No official photo. WARNING: the Wikipedia page titled "Tuan Le" is a different person (a poker player); do not use its photo. No endorsements or donor reporting found. I did not open the underlying Vox restaurant story, only the outlet and Florida Politics summaries of it. Owner sources: one combined web search (name plus the owner-source domains) returned no hits on any of them, but the search tool did not honor the site: filter, so coverage is incomplete; alexjoneslive.com on-site search also returned no results.
